messages.author: c741ce4b2ad28524
messages.subject: Noise term in glm-type models
parts:
Hi
Someone (Håvard?) mentioned once that INLA will always include the eps(i) term in the latent process model (eq 1 in the 2009 paper)
but that this term can be be approximated to zero (which I would like to do in a glm-type model) by specifying the precision to be very high.
Is this still the case, and if so, how does one specify this option in the code?
Geir

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: Noise term in glm-type models
parts:
Hi,
yes, this is still the case.  You can accomplish this by specifying the fixed high precision via the control.data parameter in your call to the inla function:

... = inla(..., family="gaussian", control.data=list(initial=10,fixed=TRUE))

This specifies a fixed precision = exp(10)

/Finn

messages.author: c741ce4b2ad28524
messages.subject: Re: Noise term in glm-type models
parts:
Thanks, Finn, but what if family="poisson"? In that case I get the error message
result = inla(formula,family="poisson", data = wdata,control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE),control.compute=list(dic=TRUE),control.data=list(initial=10,fixed=TRUE))
Error in inla.set.hyper(family[i.family], "likelihood", cont.data[[i.family]]$hyper,  :
  Modelpoisson[likelihood], has none hyperparameters, but 'initial' is 10
Does this indicate that for a poisson model the eps(i) is not included?
Geir

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Noise term in glm-type models
parts:
Ah, now I see the misconception; no, eps(i) is _not_ added to all models; it is simply the Gaussian error in a Gaussian observation equation, so it is only present for family="normal".

(disclaimer: I'm not sure if there, for numerical reasons, is a small perturbation of all models, but that would only be an implementation detail, and not visible in the results)

Finn

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Noise term in glm-type models
parts:
On Wed, 2012-02-15 at 08:50 +0100, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> Ah, now I see the misconception; no, eps(i) is _not_ added to all
> models; it is simply the Gaussian error in a Gaussian observation
> equation, so it is only present for family="normal".
>
> (disclaimer: I'm not sure if there, for numerical reasons, is a small
> perturbation of all models, but that would only be an implementation
> detail, and not visible in the results)

small noise is always added when the linear predictor is constructed and
the behaviour is controled in 'control.predictor';
see ?control.predictor

the 'linear predictor' has one hyperparameter that has the following
(non-obvious) default values:

> inla.model.properties("predictor", "predictor")$hyper
$theta
$theta$name
[1] "log precision"
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$short.name
[1] "prec"
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$initial
[1] 11
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$fixed
[1] TRUE
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$prior
[1] "loggamma"
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$param
[1] 1e+00 1e-05
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] FALSE

$theta$to.theta
function (x)
log(x)
<environment: 0x63a71f0>
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] TRUE

$theta$from.theta
function (x)
exp(x)
<environment: 0x63a71f0>
attr(,"inla.read.only")
[1] TRUE

so the precision is default fixed and set to exp(11).

in most cases this is not something you want change or tune, unless
your're in a special case where the model is scaled very badly (but then
its better to rescale the data/model...).

if you have one unique component of an "iid" model added to each
component of the linear predictor, like

y ~ ... + f(idx, model="iid") + ...

where idx=1:n, say, then you can instead make the fixed precision for
the noise in the linear predictor, random, by removing f(idx...),

y ~ ... + ....

and then add

inla(...., control.predictor = list(hyper = list(prec = list(fixed =
FALSE)))


or using the old-style

inla(..., control.predictor = list(fixed=FALSE)))

this will reduce the model-size, but I'm not sure its worth while,
really....
